en: II · Temporality of Potential, Potentiality of Time
zh: II · 潜能的时间性，时间的潜在性

en:
We are unable … in general, to think the stationary in time,
the coexistence of which with the variable, produces the conception of change.
— Immanuel Kant
zh:
一般而言，我们无法……思考时间中的持存者；
正是它与可变者的共存，产生了变化概念。
——伊曼努尔·康德

en: In the first part of the book, we tried to get a clear view of the genesis and significance of the terribly contemporary idea of the ‘end of History’. In order to do so, we had to define – approximately, of course, though not only in the vaguest terms – what it was that here supposedly met its end. We can only explain the ‘end of History’, this spirit so characteristic of our epoch (thus in itself providing a historical index), through a fundamental investigation of the very concept of

. That is, we can only explain the ‘end of History’ if we devote ourselves to naming the fundamental conditions that give a ‘historical’ character to so-called ‘historical events’, and, indeed, all the aspects – even the least evident ones – of experience. To call into question the concept of historicity entails – has entailed – a considerable expansion of our research horizons. Indeed, how can we give account of historical time, of its peculiar status, emergence and eventual decline, without encroaching on at least some of the prominent hypotheses on the structure of temporality in general?
zh: 本书第一部分试图清楚把握“历史终结”这个极具当代性的观念之生成和意义。为此，我们必须界定这里据说走向终结的究竟是什么——当然只能作近似界定，但也不能只说得含糊不清。只有从根本上考察历史性这一概念本身，我们才能解释“历史终结”——这个如此鲜明地标示我们时代、因而自身便构成一个历史指标的时代精神。也就是说，只有致力于为那些赋予所谓“历史事件”、乃至经验的所有面向（甚至最不明显的面向）以“历史”性质的根本条件命名，我们才能解释“历史终结”。质疑历史性概念，意味着——也已经意味着——大幅扩展我们的研究视野。事实上，如果不进入关于一般时间性结构的若干重要假说，我们怎么可能说明历史时间，说明它独特的地位、涌现以及最终的衰退？

en: It is possible that a certain number of readers will not have noticed the gradual widening of our field of enquiry. Or worse, that they have suffered it impatiently, considering it an error that has spoiled and dulled an otherwise lively and stimulating discussion. If they are kind-spirited, they will have considered the analysis of the déjà vu an amusing aside or impressionistic sketch. Patience, now: there is never any lack of those who look but do not see. But of course, the following pages are not addressed to

this type of reader. The rest of the book is directed, rather, towards those who have well understood what is at stake here, and are determined not to allow the author to get away with a cut-price response. To those people, that is, who would far prefer an out-in-the-open failure to the art of using a few savvy allusions in order to give off the impression of confidence. To those, that is, who are demanding that I provide a more solid foundation for the theses that have flickered across so far, as well as a detailed discussion of their implications. To unforgiving or even malevolent readers who know, however, how many nuances and hesitations are necessary in order to get straight to the point.
zh: 或许有些读者没有注意到我们的探究领域在逐渐扩展。更糟糕的是，他们可能不耐烦地忍受着这种扩展，把它看成一个错误，认为它败坏并冲淡了一场本来生动而刺激的讨论。倘若他们心地宽厚，就会把既视现象的分析看作一段有趣的离题话，或一幅印象主义速写。请耐心些：看而不见的人从来不少。不过，下面的篇章当然不是写给这类读者的。本书余下部分所面对的，是那些清楚明白问题利害所在、并决心不让作者用廉价回答蒙混过关的人；是那些宁愿看到一场明明白白的失败，也不愿看到作者用几句精明暗示制造胸有成竹假象的人；是那些要求我为迄今若隐若现的命题提供更坚实基础，并详细讨论其含义的人；是那些不肯宽恕甚至心怀恶意，却又知道为了直达要点需要多少细微限定和迟疑的读者。

: indeed, this was out of the conviction that this basic mnestic phenomenon reveals in an exemplary way the nature of historical time, or opens the door to a particularly appropriate way of accessing the historicity of experience. We drew concentric circles of ever-greater diameter around this starting point in order to unravel the various threads that make up its weft. Let us again turn our attention to the thickest of these threads. To remember the present means considering the ‘now’ as a ‘back then’, thus immersing it in a
past (a formal, indefinite, non-chronological one). This past, within which memory situates the event that we are living right now,
the potential, or faculty, underlying that same event (language, if it is a matter of dialogue; labour-power, if we are talking about the production process; etc.); conversely, potential

a non-chronological, indefinite, formal past. The memory of the present allows us, then, to grasp within the event now underway both the act and the potential, both the generic faculty and its specific execution.
zh: 前面各页的出发点是对当下的记忆，因为我们相信，这一基本记忆现象以典范方式揭示了历史时间的性质，或者为我们打开了一条极其适合通向经验之历史性的道路。我们围绕这个出发点画出直径越来越大的同心圆，以便拆解构成其经纬的不同线索。现在，让我们再次关注其中最粗的一根。记住当下，意味着把“现在”看成“那时”，从而把它沉入一种独特的过去——一种形式的、不定的、非年代性的过去。记忆把我们此刻正在经历的事件安置到这个过去中；这个过去就是同一事件所依赖的潜能或官能（如果是对话，就是语言；如果谈论生产过程，就是劳动力；等等）。反过来，潜能就是一种非年代的、不定而形式的过去。因此，对当下的记忆使我们能够在当前事件中同时把握实现与潜能、一般官能与其具体实行。

en: In this reasoning, the most delicate point, the point charged with most consequences, is without doubt the

children: equivalence drawn between past and potential

en: . Obviously such an equivalence does not leave unaltered the terms with which it is working. It immediately poses the question: how is it possible to transform the very concept of potential, now that it has been radically temporalised? And then: what weight does this non-chronological past – constituted by potential

have within our general conception of temporality? We left these two questions in the background, however, largely neglected. The reason is a simple one: the equivalence drawn between past and potential, rather than the fruit of an autonomous reflection, in fact appeared right in the middle of an analysis with a quite separate centre of gravity. It was not much more, indeed, than an auxiliary intermediate link in the chain that was destined to connect critically the pathology of the déjà vu with the supposed ‘end of History’. So what is perhaps the most important wall in the entire edifice, ended up declining to the point that it looked like a mere ornament.
zh: 在这套论证中，最微妙、也最具深远影响的环节，无疑是过去与潜能之间建立的等价关系。显然，这种等价关系不会让参与其中的两个概念保持原状。它立刻提出一个问题：既然潜能概念已经被彻底时间化，我们应当如何改造它？随之还有：由潜能本身构成的这个非年代过去，在我们关于一般时间性的理解中具有什么分量？不过，我们先前把这两个问题留在背景，几乎没有处理。原因很简单：过去与潜能之间的等价关系并非独立反思的成果，而是在一项重心完全不同的分析中途出现的。它不过是链条中的一个辅助性中间环节，而这条链条注定要把既视感病理同所谓“历史终结”批判性地连接起来。于是，或许是整座建筑中最重要的墙，反倒退居次要地位，看起来像一件纯粹装饰。

en: It seemed possible to tolerate this inconvenience, when we had to express a rather complex conceptual constellation concerning historical time, all in one breath and without gaps. But it was, still, an inconvenience: one that might encourage, or provide justification for, certain misunderstandings. It could be believed, for example, that potential coincided with the past, or became vested in a temporal aura, only because it became an object of memory within the memory of the present. As we will see, the exact opposite is the case: only because potential is, in itself, past, does it appear as an example of the mnestic phenomenon of the memory
of the present. In order to avoid such ambiguities – if for no other reason – it now seems opportune to turn the order of our reasoning upside-down, such as to put it back on its feet.
zh: 当我们必须一气呵成、毫无断裂地表达一组涉及历史时间的复杂概念时，这个麻烦似乎尚可容忍。但它毕竟是麻烦，可能鼓励某些误解，或为其提供理由。例如，人们可能以为，潜能之所以同过去重合、之所以披上一层时间光晕，只是因为它在对当下的记忆中成为记忆对象。我们将会看到，事实正好相反：只有因为潜能本身就是过去，它才会在‘对当下的记忆’这一记忆现象中显现出来。即使只为了避免这类歧义，现在也适宜把我们的论证次序整个倒转，使它重新双脚着地。

en: First of all we should explicitly and systematically define the temporal dimension of potential (a faculty, language, etc.). As we have already mentioned, however, in defining its temporal dimension we are, in effect, significantly reformulating this concept itself. The second step consists of demonstrating how and why the past
potential (or – but it is the same thing – potential

past) represents that ‘originary time’ – the foundation of the habitual chronological sequence – which contemporary philosophy has instead identified with the future. Only at this point will we begin to confront the theme of historicity, now on a wider scale and on a different basis. What, in the last analysis, is a

? What role do presence and non-actuality play in this, and how about concomitance and diachrony? Besides: is Heidegger’s view, that history is rooted in death, really plausible? The answer to these questions should prepare the terrain for our subsequent discussion on historical materialism: better, on the paths that we should beat in order to defend its corner and to fulfil its promise.
zh: 首先，我们应当明确而系统地界定潜能（官能、语言，等等）的时间维度。不过，我们已经提到：界定其时间维度，实际上就是对潜能概念本身作重大重述。第二步，是证明作为潜能的过去——或者说作为过去的潜能，二者含义相同——如何以及为什么代表那种作为惯常年代序列之基础的“本源时间”（originary time）；当代哲学却把本源时间认作未来。只有到了这一步，我们才会在更大的尺度和不同基础上重新面对历史性主题。归根结底，什么是历史时刻？在其中，在场与非现实性、并存与历时分别发挥什么作用？此外，海德格尔关于历史扎根于死亡的看法真的可信么？对这些问题的回答，应当为我们随后讨论历史唯物主义——更准确地说，为探索那些用来捍卫它并兑现其承诺的道路——准备地基。

zh: 再说一遍：下面的讨论将以不同的节奏，重新走过本书第一部分处理的问题。不言而喻，任何真正的重新考察都会引入额外问题、新命题和此前遭到忽视的视角。但同样真实的是：只有当这些由叙述语域变化所允许的进一步发展，使我们认出前面各页已经存在的东西；只有当它们最终证明自己恰恰而且仅仅是对这些问题的重新考察——无论表面证据看起来多么相反——它们才算达成目的。
